text: Profit up two hundred twenty three percent. But Manna-puram fell almost five percent this week. Multibagger, or trap?
Manna-puram Finance is a gold loan company from Kerala. You pledge your gold jewellery, and get cash in minutes. Pay back with interest, and take your gold home.
And gold loans are booming. Its gold loan book almost doubled in one year, from thirty one thousand five hundred crore, to sixty thousand six hundred forty crore.
Then a big global investor walked in. Bain Capital put in four thousand three hundred eighty five crore rupees, and now runs the company along with the founders.
Latest results. Profit jumped from two hundred seventeen crore, to seven hundred one crore. That's more than three times.
But here's the catch. A year ago, its microfinance arm, Aashirvaad, lost one hundred sixty eight crore. This quarter, it made thirty two crore. So part of that jump is just a bad year going away.
And gold loans ride on the gold price. If gold falls, the gold behind every loan is worth less. The stock is already twenty six percent below its high of three hundred eighty one.
So, multibagger or trap? Right now, the business is strong. But it rides on gold. Watch the gold price, and watch Aashirvaad.
Save this, and send it to your friend who holds Manna-puram. Education only, not investment advice. Follow money in cloud.
